title: Energy demand
content: Energy demand is the consumption of energy by human activities.
e: Energy demand is the energy consumed by human activities. It is the quantity a country actually uses, not the size of the resource in the ground.

title: Energy crisis
content: Energy crisis is the concern that the world's demands on the limited natural resources that are used to power industrial society are diminishing as the demand rises.
e: An energy crisis is the worry that industrial demand on limited natural fuels is rising while those fuels diminish. Supply then cannot keep up safely.

title: Non-renewable energy
content: A non-renewable energy is a natural substance that is not replenished with the speed at which it is consumed.
e: A non-renewable energy source is a natural store that is not replenished as fast as we consume it. Once it is gone on a human timescale, it is gone.

title: Renewable energy sources
content: Renewable energy sources (also called non-conventional energy sources) are continuously replenished by natural processes.
e: Renewable sources, also called non-conventional sources, are continuously replenished by natural processes. Sunlight, wind, falling water and biomass sit in this group.

title: Solar energy
content: Solar energy is the radiant light and heat from the sun that has been harnessed by humans since ancient times using a range of ever-evolving technologies.
e: Solar energy is the Sun's radiant light and heat, harnessed with evolving technology. Using it does not use up the Sun.

title: Photovoltaic effect
content: Conversion of light energy into electrical energy is based on a phenomenon called photovoltaic effect.
e: The photovoltaic effect converts light energy into electrical energy. Photons free electrons in a semiconductor; heat is not the working idea here.

title: Wind energy
content: Wind energy is the energy generated or produced by harnessing the power of the wind.
e: Wind energy is the energy obtained by harnessing the power of moving air. Turbines convert that kinetic energy into electricity.

title: Hydroelectric energy
content: The flowing water and water stored in huge dams is also very important source of energy which is known as a hydroelectric energy.
e: Hydroelectric energy comes from flowing water and water stored in dams. Gravity does the work as water falls through a turbine.

title: Geothermal energy
content: Geothermal energy is a type of renewable energy taken from the earth's core (the internal heat of the earth) and it is one of the oldest types of natural sources of heat.
e: Geothermal energy is renewable heat taken from the Earth's interior. It is Earth's own heat, not sunlight collected at the surface.

title: Fossil fuels
content: Fossil fuels, such as coal, oil and natural gases, are important non-renewable sources of energy.
e: Fossil fuels such as coal, oil and natural gas are important non-renewable energy stores. They formed from ancient remains over geological time.

title: Acid rain
content: Acid rain is caused by a chemical reaction that begins when compounds like sulfur dioxide and nitrogen oxides are released into the air. These substances can rise very high into the atmosphere, where they mix and react with water, oxygen, and other chemicals to form more acidic pollutants, known as acid rain.
e: Acid rain starts when SO₂ and NOₓ rise into the air and react with water, oxygen and other chemicals. The acidic pollutants then corrode buildings, soil and forests.

title: Solar cell
content: A solar cell (also known as photovoltaic cell) is defined as an electrical device that converts light energy into electrical energy through the photovoltaic effect.
e: A solar cell, or photovoltaic cell, converts light into electricity by the photovoltaic effect. It is not a chemical battery that stores charge by itself.

title: Coalification
content: Coal is formed in a way similar to the other fossil fuels, though it goes through a different process called coalification.
e: Coal forms like other fossil fuels but through a distinct process called coalification. The deposit type then sets the grade of the coal.

title: Methane
content: Methane is a common gas found in swamps and is also the by-product of animals' digestive system.
e: Methane is a common swamp gas and a by-product of animal digestion. It is also the main molecule in natural gas.

title: Nuclear energy
content: Nuclear energy is non-renewable energy as the uranium fuels used are consumed in the nuclear fission reaction and hence are non-replenishable.
e: Nuclear energy is classed as non-renewable because the uranium fuel is consumed in fission and is not replenished. Do not mix that with sunlight or wind.

title: Irradiance
content: The total amount of radiation energy passing through per unit area and per unit time is called irradiance.
e: Irradiance is the radiation energy passing through unit area in unit time. For sunlight that flux is also called insolation.

title: Solar panels
content: Individual solar cells can be combined to form modules commonly known as solar panels.
e: Individual solar cells are combined into modules commonly called solar panels. A single cell is too small for a rooftop array.

title: Biomass
content: Biomass is renewable organic material that comes from plants and animals.
e: Biomass is renewable organic material from plants and animals. It is not a mineral fossil fuel, even though it can be burned.
